# {{PLAN_NAME}} — execution protocol

What is being built and why lives in `PLAN.md`, next to this file. This file says **how the work is done**.

**How to start:** in an agent session opened at the repository root, `/plan-relay:plan {{PLAN_NAME}}` shows the progress, what is in progress and for how long, and offers the choice of the next task; `/plan-relay:plan {{PLAN_NAME}} <ID>` runs or resumes a task.

The work is split into phases, and phases into tasks that fit in one or two agent sessions. Each task stands on its own: it says what to read, what to deliver, how to prove it is finished and where the next session picks up, even days later and with no memory of this one.

{{#full}}
`spec/` is the source of truth for what is being built; the task says what to do now. When the two disagree, the spec wins, and the disagreement goes into the task's `## Log` or becomes an edit to the spec.
{{/full}}
{{#lean}}
`PLAN.md` is the source of truth for what is being built; the task says what to do now. When the two disagree, `PLAN.md` wins, and the disagreement goes into the task's `## Log` or becomes an edit to `PLAN.md`.
{{/lean}}

## Layout

```
{{PLAN_PATH}}/
  README.md         <- this protocol
{{#full}}
  PLAN.md           <- what it is, principles, phases, out of scope
{{/full}}
{{#lean}}
  PLAN.md           <- what it is, principles, phases, decisions, out of scope
{{/lean}}
  MAP.md            <- every task by phase and the critical path (generated by map.sh)
  _template.md      <- the shape of a task
  plan.json         <- name, source document and contract version
  status.sh         <- progress, in progress (and for how long), available, parallel sessions, blocked; --json for machines
  task.sh           <- changes the state of a task: claim, close, release, cancel, giveup, reopen
  map.sh            <- rewrites MAP.md from the headers
{{#full}}
  spec/             <- what is being built; decisions in spec/decisions.md
  research/         <- cited research (P01, P02...)
  prototypes/       <- throwaway sketches; only the lessons move into the spec
{{/full}}
  notes/            <- measurements and long findings; the autopilot journal in notes/run-YYYY-MM-DD.md
  phase-N-<slug>/   <- PHASE.md and the tasks of the phase
```

Paths cited in tasks are relative to the repository root.

Phases set the order of priority; what decides whether a task can start is only its `Blocked by:` line. Tasks with no edge between them run in parallel, in different sessions, in any order.

## Header

Every task opens with the roles block, before the title, and `Status:` is always the first line:

```
Status: ready
Type: code
Track: <track>
Tier: mid
Repos: <repo-a>, <repo-b>
Blocked by: F1-02, F0-02

# F1-03 - <title>
```

- **Status:** `draft` (goal and edges written, steps still to detail; not started) · `ready` · `in-progress` · `done` · `cancelled` (replaced by another task by the agent; reason in the `## Log`) · `abandoned` (the owner gave it up, or gave up a task it depended on; reason in the root's `## Log`). The last two leave the total and never count as a resolved blocker. See [Cancel, give up and reopen](#cancel-give-up-and-reopen).
- **Replaced by:**, **Given up by:**, **Given up with:** and **Previous status:** written by `task.sh` on cancel and give up. Never by hand.
- **Type:** see [Types](#types).
- **Track:** the thread of work, to filter `status.sh`.
- **Tier:** `junior`, `mid` or `senior`, by the criteria in [Tiers](#tiers). Leave it out on `human` tasks.
- **Repos:** the repositories the task changes; `status.sh` uses them to suggest parallel sessions without conflict. Leave it out when it changes none.
- **Blocked by:** comma-separated IDs. Leave it out when there are none.
- **Started:** and **Finished:** (UTC) written by `task.sh`. Never by hand.

The keys, the values and the markers (`## Done when`, `## Log`, `Next step:`) are the contract the scripts read: they stay in English, as here. The rest of the task text follows the language of the plan.

`Status:` changes only through `task.sh`. `MAP.md` holds no state; `status.sh` computes everything from the headers.

### Tiers

`Tier:` says how much judgment the task needs. The autopilot conductor launches each tier on a model and, if a worker below `senior` fails, relaunches the task once as `senior`.

- **`junior`:** mechanical work already decided, with up to ~5 files in the deliverables and short reading.
- **`mid`:** implementation with a clear spec and nothing left to decide; text for people (README, CONTRIBUTING, store page); replacement from a list, even across the whole repository; a measurement or experiment with an external tool whose result does not decide the way forward.
- **`senior`:** `decision`, `research`, `prototype` and `review`; a decision inside the task ("decide the format", "decide whether..."); text that agents read (skills, prompts, this README); design across modules; a measurement whose result decides the way forward.
- **When in doubt, `senior`.** With no `Tier:`, or with any other value, the task counts as `senior`.
- **`human`** has no tier: the conductor does not launch it.

{{#full}}
`Tier:` is written by whoever makes the task `ready`: whoever maps the plan, for tasks born `ready`; whoever creates a task or subtask; and the end-of-phase `review` when it details a `draft` (a decision the detailing takes may lower the tier). The autopilot does not change the field; an escalation is recorded only in the journal.
{{/full}}
{{#lean}}
`Tier:` is written by whoever writes the task: whoever maps the plan and whoever creates a task or subtask. The autopilot does not change the field; an escalation is recorded only in the journal.
{{/lean}}

## Work session

1. **Choose.** The named task, or the one picked from the `/plan-relay:plan {{PLAN_NAME}}` card. *Ready when* every ID in `Blocked by:` is `done`.
2. **Claim.** `sh {{PLAN_PATH}}/task.sh claim <ID>` and open the session entry in the `## Log`, before any other work. The script refuses a task that is blocked or already in progress. If it was already `in-progress`, read the `## Log` and resume from the `Next step:`.
3. **Read.** What is under "Read first" and the `## Log` of each task in `Blocked by:`. Upstream decisions apply here.
{{#full}}
4. **Execute.** Follow the steps. Code is born test-first: the test of the rule goes red, the code makes it green, and only then is it refactored.
{{/full}}
{{#lean}}
4. **Execute.** Follow the steps. The tests the task asks for are part of the delivery.
{{/lean}}
5. **Evaluate.** Go through the "Evaluation points" and apply the action of each one.
6. **Verify.** Run each item of the `## Done when` and tick `[x]` only what was verified in this session.
7. **Self-review.** Reread the work as a reviewer: was the criterion proved or only asserted? Did the task rest on assumptions the code contradicts? Did a task further on get harder or easier — then its text or its `Blocked by:` changes now.
8. **Close.** Complete the `## Log` and run `sh {{PLAN_PATH}}/task.sh close <ID>`, which refuses while there is a `- [ ]` in the `## Done when`.

**A session that gives up before changing anything:** `sh {{PLAN_PATH}}/task.sh release <ID>`.
**An interrupted session:** `Status:` stays `in-progress` and the `## Log` ends in a concrete `Next step:`. `status.sh` warns when it is missing.

`## Log` entry:

```
### <YYYY-MM-DD> — session <n>
- Done: ...
- Decisions: ... (what and why; includes the answers of whoever decides)
- Surprises: ...
- Commits: <repo> <hash> — <first line>
- Subtasks created: <ID> — <reason>
- Next step: ... (required while in-progress)
```

### Cancel, give up and reopen

- **Cancelling belongs to the agent:** the task no longer makes sense as written. `sh {{PLAN_PATH}}/task.sh cancel <ID> --reason "<reason>"` refuses while there is a live dependent, and names it; it never cancels in cascade. With dependents: create the replacement (through [Subtasks](#subtasks), usually with the old `Blocked by:`), swap the old ID for the new one in the `Blocked by:` of each dependent, and only then cancel with `--replaced-by <replacement>`. The autopilot cancels only this way, by replacement.
- **Giving up belongs to the owner:** it takes the task out of the plan together with everything that depended on it, in cascade and across phases. The agent never gives up on its own. `sh {{PLAN_PATH}}/task.sh giveup <ID>` shows what would fall (with `--json`, for machines) and changes nothing; only after the owner has seen that list and said "yes" does `giveup <ID> --reason "<reason>" --yes` apply it. The root gets `Given up by: owner`, and the tasks that fell with it, `Given up with: <root>`.
- **Reopening undoes a give-up,** as a group and only when the owner asks: `sh {{PLAN_PATH}}/task.sh reopen <root>` puts the root and the tasks that fell with it back to `ready` or `draft`. A cancelled task is not reopened.
- **The reason** is required by `cancel` and `giveup --yes`, one only, and goes to the `## Log`: the root's gets the whole sentence; each task that fell with it gets "abandoned together with <root>". It is refused when empty, or when every word is a single character (`-`, `aaa`, `--- 1`).

## Types

- **code:** the agent implements and tests.
{{#full}}
- **research:** the agent investigates against primary sources and delivers `research/Pnn-<slug>.md`, one source per claim and `[?]` on what was not confirmed.
- **prototype:** a throwaway sketch in `prototypes/<name>/` answers concrete questions; the lessons go into the spec.
- **decision:** the agent lays out the options, with cost and consequence, and asks; the choice belongs to whoever decides. It goes into `spec/decisions.md` and the `## Log`.
{{/full}}
{{#lean}}
- **decision:** the agent lays out the options, with cost and consequence, and asks; the choice belongs to whoever decides. It goes into the "Decisions" section of `PLAN.md` and the `## Log`.
{{/lean}}
- **human:** steps only a person can take (access, requests to other teams, licenses). The agent prepares the script and checks the result without seeing secrets.
{{#full}}
- **review:** the agent runs or inspects something real and gives each finding a destination: a fix within scope or a subtask. Every phase closes with a `review` that details the `draft` tasks of the next phase, writes the `Tier:` of each one and moves them to `ready`.
{{/full}}
{{#lean}}
- **review:** the agent runs or inspects something real and gives each finding a destination: a fix within scope or a subtask. A phase closes with a `review` only when what it delivers calls for that check.
{{/lean}}

## Subtasks

A task creates a subtask when an evaluation point says so, when necessary work shows up that is out of scope and bigger than an adjustment, or when part of the work waits on a decision that did not come in this session. Work that fits in the scope is done in the task itself.

1. **ID and file.** The parent's ID with `.n`: `F1-03.1`; a subtask of a subtask is `F1-03.1.1`. Same folder as the parent, from `_template.md`, with `Status: ready`.
2. **Complete content,** written for a session that has not seen this one.
3. **Edges.** `grep -l "^Blocked by:.*F1-03" {{PLAN_PATH}}/phase-*/*.md` lists who depends on the parent; whoever needs what the subtask produces gets it in `Blocked by:`. That is how a step further on gets blocked.
4. **Map.** `sh {{PLAN_PATH}}/map.sh`.
5. **Record.** Note the created subtask and why in the parent's `## Log`.

## Version control

When the project root is a git repository, `{{PLAN_PATH}}/` is versioned with the code, unless the conventions below say otherwise. Commits name the files one by one, never `git add -A` or `git add .`: parallel sessions may be touching other tasks. No commit leaves the machine without the owner.

- **Mapping.** `/plan-relay:map` ends with a commit of `{{PLAN_PATH}}/`.
{{#full}}
- **Work session.** The deliverables go in the commit (or commits) that the "Commits:" line of the `## Log` cites. After `task.sh close` — or, in an interrupted session, after the `Next step:` is written —, a separate commit with the plan files the session changed: the task, the subtasks it created, `MAP.md`, and what it wrote in `spec/`, `research/`, `prototypes/` and `notes/`. It is separate because the `## Log`, which goes in it, cannot cite its own hash.
{{/full}}
{{#lean}}
- **Work session.** The deliverables go in the commit (or commits) that the "Commits:" line of the `## Log` cites. After `task.sh close` — or, in an interrupted session, after the `Next step:` is written —, a separate commit with the plan files the session changed: the task, the subtasks it created, `MAP.md`, and what it wrote in `PLAN.md` and in `notes/`. It is separate because the `## Log`, which goes in it, cannot cite its own hash.
{{/lean}}
- **Autopilot.** The conductor commits the journal (`notes/run-*.md`) in `## Closing` and in `## Handoff`.

Outside a git repository, none of this applies.
